title: Reduce CPU syscalls and thread handoff on request path
author: Aisha Kumar
description: Motivation: CPU-side bottlenecks on the request hot path were dominated by frequent syscalls and expensive thread handoffs when requests crossed the network/IO boundary. This PR reduces syscall frequency and simplifies handoff between acceptor/dispatcher threads and worker pools to lower tail latency and overall CPU usage. Summary of approach: 1) Replace a large fraction of blocking read()/write()/select() syscalls on the hot path with an edge-triggered epoll-based poll loop + per-core submission queues to amortize kernel transitions; 2) Introduce a light-weight per-core MPMC ring buffer (lock-free where supported) used to hand off ready requests to CPU-local worker shards instead of parking/unparking threads; 3) Move request serialization (marshalling) off the acceptor path onto a short-lived serialization worker that batches small requests together (continuous batching window = 1.5ms configurable) to reduce per-request syscall and kernel scheduling pressure; 4) Make KV cache lookups prefetch-friendly and avoid cacheline thrash by introducing per-shard micro-ttl caches and partitioned LRU lists; 5) Reduce futex/wake cycles by aggregating wake events using a shared event-coalescer and using eventfd on Linux where available. Results: On our internal bench (conv1k latency-heavy mix) we see a 28-35% reduction in 99th percentile CPU time spent in syscall/wakeup handling and a 12-18% improvement in overall token throughput on c5d-large simulation (worker-limited). Tail latency (p99.9) decreased by ~9% for small requests (<128 tokens). Backwards compatibility and safety: All changes are behind a feature flag (runtime.enable_syscall_reduction) and fall back to the original path when disabled. New primitives are exercised via unit + integration tests, and we added a runtime smoke test that toggles the feature flag under load. Details of changes: commits, files touched, and notes below.

small_snippets: +++ runtime/threading/submission_ring.h: added lock-free MPMC ring API (try_push/try_pop)
- blocking acceptor path: used to call notify_worker() on every socket event
+ new path: push descriptor into per-core ring; worker polls ring and performs a single epoll_wait for batched sockets
review_comments: Marcus Lee: Please add a comment explaining why the ring is bounded and how capacity is chosen; also add metrics for ring-full events.
Aisha Kumar: Added ring capacity metric and docs; default chosen as 4096 entries after load tuning.
Sofia Ramos: Concern about priority inversion when heavy serialization batches starve small low-latency requests. Please add a max-batch-bytes and an override path for urgent requests.

benchmarks: baseline: throughput 14.3k tokens/s, p99 handler latency 68ms
this PR: throughput 16.2k tokens/s (+13.3%), p99 handler latency 62ms (-8.8%), syscall CPU cost -31%
notes_on_porting: Feature flag runtime.enable_syscall_reduction defaults to false for now; enable via console or env var REDWOOD_SYSFLAG_SYSCALL_REDUCTION=1
Windows: eventfd path is no-op; the fallback uses WaitForMultipleObjects with coalescing logic. See runtime/net/poller_win.cpp
Observability: added metrics submission_ring_push_failures, batcher_avg_size, ring_fill_percent per-core
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: ring full during sudden traffic spikes -> drop to fallback path (original acceptor) and emit metric. Mitigation: metric-driven autoscale and conservative default ring size.
Risk: batching could increase latency for single-request workloads -> mitigated via small default batching window (1.5ms) and urgent bypass flag.
Risk: lock-free primitives subtle on older kernels/arch -> guarded by runtime.use_lockfree_rings; we fall back to mutex-backed queue on unsupported archs.
release_notes: Performance: Reduced kernel-transition overhead on the request path by introducing per-core submission queues, coalesced event wakeups, and configurable continuous batching. Enabled behind runtime.enable_syscall_reduction.
merge_outcome: Merged via squash by Marcus Lee after approvals. All CI green and perf guardrails met.
backcompat: No API changes. Feature gated and defaults preserved. Config docs updated in docs/feature_flags.md.
testing: Unit tests for ring buffer and batch marshaller added; integration test toggles feature flag under load; perf harness run nightly for 2 weeks pre-merge.
